source_text: Type III, involving narrowing of the vaginal opening through excision and apposition of the labia, carries elevated immediate harm risks compared to Types I and II, including higher urine retention (median 31%) and potential for keloids, yet long-term physical health data indicate that deinfibulation or natural adaptation allows many women to maintain functionality without recurrent infections or fistulae. [33]
